name: gdc-organoid-pancreatic
description:
Patient-derived organoids occupy a useful middle ground: they retain patient-specific genomics while remaining experimentally tractable, which tissue cohorts are not. This resource profiles 70 pancreatic cancer organoids with exome sequencing on 69, RNA sequencing on 49 and whole genome on 22, with stage recorded for 84% of the source tumors.
Its distinctive value is that the source publication paired these molecular profiles with pharmacotyping - measured drug responses - which makes it one of the few NCI resources where genotype can be related to an experimentally measured phenotype rather than to a clinical outcome recorded years later.
citeAs: Organoid Profiling Identifies Common Responders to Chemotherapy in Pancreatic Cancer

supportedQuestions: Which molecular features predict chemotherapy sensitivity in pancreatic cancer organoids?
How faithfully do organoids recapitulate the genomics of the tumors they came from?
Can organoid expression programs stratify pancreatic cancer subtypes established in tissue cohorts?

blockingLimitations.statement: Vital status is populated for all 70 cases and informative for none, and progression is likewise uninformative. No clinical outcome endpoint exists in these records.

inappropriateUses: Claiming clinical efficacy from organoid drug response.
